parsed.why: No visitor-facing criminalisation; courts actively protect trans people (police-advice ruling, no-surgery ruling, posthumous military reinstatement). Downsides: no anti-discrimination law, hospitalisation gap, Pride violence, contact-tracing doxing. Capital LGBTQ districts positive.

Decriminalised, constitutional gender-identity protection, culturally embedded third-gender identity, no documented police targeting of trans visitors. Weighed against conservative religious climate, one 2018 trans killing, no recognition route, weak reporting trust, unimplemented protections.

No marker-change route ever (8/8 rejections), same-sex unions rejected, DV law excludes same-sex partners, no constitutional SOGI ground, official and media hostility. No criminalisation or documented violence, but thin record and no operating protections for outed visitors.

State hostile: birth-sex prison placement with documented sexual assault, femicide exclusion justified officially, bias crimes tolerated, anti-trans legislative agenda, normalised conversion practices with electroshock. No criminalisation and no recent trans killing, but hostility reaches institutions.

Criminalised: five-year minimum for any homosexual act, mandatory terms, arrests and police harassment documented; 93% social hostility, religious calls for killing, no LGBT organisations. Gender-nonconforming visitors face police and societal threat with no recourse.
